data.name: GameMode_Classic_Description
data.value: Twister as you know it. Events only if you pick a set yourself.

data.name: GameMode_Classic_Rules
data.value:
The app calls a player, then after a moment gives a limb and a colour. Put that limb on a free circle of that colour and hold it there.
You move to the next turn yourself — with the „Next” button or by voice. In automatic mode (switch it on in settings) the turn changes on its own after the set time.
Events are up to you: if you picked an event set, events will fire during the game. With no set chosen you play classic Twister, moves only.
The app knocks out nobody — when a player falls, press the button next to their name. The last person standing wins.

data.name: GameMode_Hardcore_Description
data.value: Harder sequences, frequent events and half the time.

data.name: GameMode_Hardcore_Rules
data.value:
The same base rules as Classic, with three differences.
Moves are picked to be as awkward as possible: the same limb is almost never called twice in a row, repeats are pushed far apart and a move that changes nothing is practically excluded.
Events fire much more often and can come in consecutive turns.
There is half the time: this mode cuts both the move time and the task time to 50% of the value from settings. In manual mode that applies to event tasks, in automatic mode also to the move time.
You move to the next turn with a button or by voice — unless you switch on automatic mode.

data.name: GameMode_Kids_Description
data.value: Gentle moves, more time and nobody is knocked out.

data.name: GameMode_Kids_Rules
data.value:
The same base rules as Classic, with one important difference: **nobody is eliminated**. A fall costs nothing, the game simply continues, and there is no elimination button next to the players' names.
Moves are easier: the same limb and the same colour may repeat, so a child does not have to twist across the whole mat.
There is half as much time again: this mode extends both the move time and the task time to 150% of the value from settings.
You move to the next turn with a button or by voice — unless you switch on automatic mode.

data.name: GameMode_Party_Description
data.value: Lots of events for a group that came to have fun.

data.name: GameMode_Party_Rules
data.value:
The same base rules as Classic, with events happening often.
Moves stay standard — the fun comes from the events, not from the difficulty of the poses. Times are as you set them.
Uses the Party event set unless you pick a different one yourself.
You move to the next turn with a button or by voice — unless you switch on automatic mode.

data.name: GameMode_Singing_Description
data.value: Events built around singing, with more time per task.

data.name: GameMode_Singing_Rules
data.value:
The same base rules as Classic, with events that ask players to sing, hum or make a sound.
The task itself gets half as much time again (150% of the value from settings), because singing a chorus takes longer than placing a hand. The move time stays unchanged.
Uses the Family set unless you pick a different one yourself — it has singing tasks in it. Works best with a set full of them.
You move to the next turn with a button or by voice — unless you switch on automatic mode.

data.name: Onboarding_Step1_Body
data.value:
Hi! This app is your helper for playing Twister — it replaces the cardboard spinner and runs the whole game for you.
Lost the spinner? No harm done. The app draws the move, calls the player by name and says out loud what to do — and you simply play.
That is what finally makes a two-player game work: nobody has to sit out and spin the wheel. There are three ways to run the game — manual, automatic and voice control. The phone can stay off the mat; you never have to reach for it.
You can also add events of your own: short tasks that drop in at random during the game and turn it upside down.
Twister® is a trademark of Hasbro. This app is unofficial and not affiliated with Hasbro or with the publisher of the game.

data.name: Onboarding_Step2_Body
data.value:
Players — enter the names of everyone joining the game. Those are the names the app will call out for each turn.
Events — pick a ready-made set or build your own, and decide how often they should drop in. You can also play without them entirely.
Game modes — classic, kids, party, hardcore. Each changes the pace and the difficulty; what exactly it does is written under “Rules”.
Settings — the voice and its speed, sounds, move time and how turns advance.
Then just open “Play” and press “Start game”. Everything you set is remembered for next time.

data.name: Onboarding_Step3_Body
data.value:
The app calls a player by name, pauses for a moment and gives the instruction: a limb and a colour. A large circle in that colour appears in the middle of the screen — put the named hand or foot on a free spot of that colour and hold it.
Below the circle a countdown ticks: that is how much time is left for the move. In manual mode the app waits for you when it runs out — the next turn starts with “Next”. In automatic mode it moves on by itself.
Whoever falls is out — tap their name on the bar below the buttons and it will be crossed out. The last person on the mat wins.
With voice control on you do not have to touch the phone at all: say “next”, “repeat”, “pause” or “resume”. A short cue tells you when the microphone is listening — one tone when it opens, a falling one when it closes.
Did not catch the instruction? “Repeat” will read it out again.
